I am an old man of 77 years, and this small piece of land I rent is all I have to feed my household. I cannot afford much fertilizer from the shop — the prices are too high for someone like me — but if the government coupon reaches me I will use a little on the maize. I keep some chickens and goats, so I spread what manure I can gather, and I intercrop with pumpkins and beans the way my father taught me. My body is tired, so my children and grandchildren help me with the hoeing and weeding; I cannot afford to pay outside people.
